reason: Funnel-form is a spelling of funnelform, which the previous review mapped to PATO:0002521 funnel-shaped (C217, C218).
Uninerved means one vein, so it is a count of veins (config/flora_counted_parts.tsv: nerved -> vein), like '5-nerved'.
A curved-ascending stem or vein rises gradually upward along a curve, which PATO:0104355 ascending already describes. The curve is not a second value of the trait.

Reclining stems lean back or lie down with rising tips. Floras put the word between erect and procumbent ('reclining or suberect', 'reclining to procumbent'), which is PATO:0002343 decumbent. Not PATO:0001965 reclinate, which is about bent-down edges.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (slot 1: part of the bearer, the apex, with its own quality)
reason: 'Tipped with crimson' or 'tipped yellow' gives the colour of the apex of the part. 'With a short tip' gives a point at the apex, so the quality is the colour or point, not 'tipped'.
An umbrella-shaped inflorescence has its flowers arising from about one point, as in an umbel: FLOPO:0991031 umbelliform (synonyms umbel-like, umbel-shaped).
'Leaves polymorphic' means the leaves vary in form, which is PATO:0001930 variant shape. FLOPO:0991092 dimorphic is the narrower two-form case.

'Fruits baccate' or 'capsules baccate' means fleshy like a berry, and PATO:0002351 fleshy is the quality. Where the text names the fruit a berry, the bearer is berry fruit (PO_0030108). 'Spore baccate' is a parsing error.

Oily leaves and surfaces ('oily sheen', 'not oily') have an oily coating: PATO:0001606 greasy. The oil content of seeds or pulp is a composition quality that PATO lacks, so those statements fit the rule less well.

label: palmatipartite
definition: A split quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being cut more than halfway, but not fully, to the base into segments radiating from a common point. NOTE: Palmate counterpart of FLOPO:0991156 pinnatipartite; sibling of FLOPO:0991160 pedate.
reason: A standard term for the depth of division of leaves, bracts and stipules. The pinnate series (pinnatifid, pinnatipartite, pinnatisect) already exists, but the palmate one does not.

label: spine-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's similarity to the appearance of a spine: rigid, narrow and sharp-pointed. NOTE: Sibling of PATO:0002457 leaf-like and FLOPO:0991200 bract-like, worded as they are. PATO:0001365 spiny is the quality of bearing spines.
reason: Spine-like bracts, stipules and branches resemble a spine without bearing spines, so PATO:0001365 spiny does not fit. 'Leaf modified into a spine' is better annotated with the bearer spine leaf (PO_0025173).
A suckering plant produces suckers, which PO lists as a synonym of root-borne shoot system PO_0004544. Suckers from a rhizome or stem base are shoot-borne (PO_0004545).
A gaping flower throat, spathe or spikelet has parts held wide apart, leaving an unobstructed opening: PATO:0000610 open.
The absence of an unnamed appendage. 'Appendage' and 'appendaged' were rejected as generic in the previous review (C182), so this needs the specific part (awn, spur, connective appendage).

target: docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md; new: alternation within a series
reason: Most uses are relational ('alternating with the petals') or describe a series ('alternately longer and shorter'). Leaves 'alternating at each node' already map to PATO:0001932 alternate placement.
A comparison stated without its second term, as for 'darker' (C242). If the other surface is named, the colour is FLOPO:0991070 discolorous.
The negation of PATO:0001847 constricted, as 'unlobed' = not lobed (C239).

label: marginate
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's edge being bordered by a distinct raised or thickened rim. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991196 crested and FLOPO:0991062 ribbed; the rim runs along the margin rather than across the surface.
reason: Achenes, seeds and sepals 'rimmed' or 'with a rim' have a raised border, a common character in Cyperaceae and Asteraceae. 'Rim' alone was rejected as a generic part (C202), so the quality needs a term.
Lineate means marked with fine, usually parallel lines: PATO:0001410 striated ('marked by narrow lines or grooves, usually parallel'). Lines of another colour can also take FLOPO:0991206 streaked.
Trigonal ovaries, fruits and seeds are three-angled: FLOPO:0991120 trigonous (as triquetrous, C362).
An eccentric midvein, style, hilum or aril is placed off the centre: the negation of PATO:0002268 centered (rule C340 for 'central'). PATO has 'eccentric' only as a RELATED synonym of ovate.
Horny pericarps, endosperms and margins are hard and tough like horn: PATO:0000386 hard (as 'indurate', C305). A horny leaf margin is close to FLOPO:0991099 cartilaginous (sensu botany).

label: bipinnatisect
definition: A pinnatisect quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being cut to the midrib into segments that are themselves cut to their midribs. NOTE: Follows FLOPO:0991155 pinnatisect, as FLOPO:0991014 bipinnate follows pinnate.
reason: A standard term for leaf division (53 statements in 11 floras). It is a kind of pinnatisect, as bipinnate is a kind of pinnate.
Mixed meanings: without colour marks (corolla), without scars or lines (petiole), and the French 'peu marqué', meaning hardly visible. With no stated marking to negate, the word is too vague.
A stony endocarp or seed is very hard: PATO:0000386 hard. PATO:0002126 osseous means containing bone and does not apply.
Weakly developed ridges, veins, horns and bristles are low and hardly evident, read like 'obscure' (C174). PATO:0000645 hypoplastic is a cell-number quality and does not fit.
Toothless = not toothed: the negation of PATO:0001205 dentated (EXACT synonym toothed), as 'unlobed' = not lobed. For leaf margins, PATO:0104359 entire is the stronger positive statement.

Enclosed peduncles, spikes, stamens and Sphagnum chlorophyllous cells do not project beyond the structure around them: FLOPO:0991121 included. The enclosing part, when named, follows docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md.
Grouped branches, spikes and megasporophylls are gathered close together: PATO:0001629 aggregated (synonyms clumped, clustered).
Nervate = nerved, i.e. with evident veins (rules C211, C212). 'Many-nerved' is a count and goes to docs/odp/03-count-of-parts.md.
